parts.label: a
parts.method: Work from the inside out: g first, then f
slips: Finding \(\mathrm{fg}(x)\) first and slipping when expanding the squared fraction.

parts.label: b
parts.method: Swap the roles: make \(x\) the subject

steps.why: Multiply both sides by \(2x - 9\) to clear the fraction.
Get the \(x\) term on its own.

steps.text: Now write it as a function of \(x\). Its domain is every value except the one that makes the denominator zero.
steps.why: The domain of \(\mathrm{g}^{-1}\) is the range of \(\mathrm{g}\): \(\dfrac{5}{2x-9}\) can never be 0.

slips: Leaving out the domain \(x \neq 0\). Examiners have pointed this out in many past reports.
Differentiating g, or finding its reciprocal \(\tfrac{2x-9}{5}\), instead of the inverse.
A sign slip with the \(9y\) term.

parts.label: c(i)
slips: Multiplying \(\mathrm{g}(x)\) by \(\mathrm{f}(x)\) instead of putting one inside the other.
Finding \(\mathrm{fg}(x)\) instead, or making an algebra slip while over-simplifying a correct answer.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.method: Find the smallest and largest the denominator can be

steps.why: The smallest denominator gives the most negative value.

steps.text: As \(x\) grows, \(1 + 6x^2\) grows without limit, so \(-\dfrac{5}{1 + 6x^2}\) gets closer to 0 but never reaches it.

slips: Giving only one end, \(\mathrm{gf}(x) \geq -5\) or \(\mathrm{gf}(x) < 0\), instead of the whole interval.
Writing the range in terms of \(x\), such as \(-5 \leq x < 0\). A range is about the output: use \(y\) or \(\mathrm{gf}(x)\).

parts.label: d
parts.ask: \(\mathrm{h}(x) = 2x^2 - 6x + k\). Find the values of \(k\) for which \(\mathrm{f}(x) = \mathrm{h}(x)\) has no real solutions.
parts.method: Form a quadratic, then use the discriminant

steps.why: Collect everything on the side where \(x^2\) is positive.

steps.text: No real solutions means the discriminant is negative: \(b^2 - 4ac < 0\).
steps.why: Not \(\leq 0\): a zero discriminant gives one repeated root.
Moving \(20k\) across avoids dividing by \(-20\), so the inequality never has to flip.

slips: Using \(b^2 - 4ac \geq 0\), the condition for real roots, instead of \(< 0\).
Slips expanding \(-4(5)(k-4)\), or dividing by \(-20\) without reversing the inequality.
Dropping the \(= 0\), or taking the discriminant of a quadratic set equal to \(k\).
